ambiguities: C2: Design Studio C/D's staged interim-to-final booklet documentation of 'iterative exploration and critical evaluation' reads toward level 3's process-focused reliance-justification anchor, but no assessed item explicitly requires documenting/justifying reliance decisions or defending AI-output judgements — resolved to level 2.

C3: Architectural Practice's (ABPL90140) core-unit outcome names AI critically ('impacts of disruptive change... artificial intelligence... on architectural practice workflows'), which is stronger than pure tool-operation content, but is not shown to be an assessed item (R2) — resolved to level 1, the level matching AI's only clearly-assessed appearance (as an elective subject).

C5: Design Thesis (ABPL90169) is a required core subject staged through three oral 'Design crit' reviews, which reads toward level 3's 'methodology defended under scrutiny (viva, defence, or staged supervised review),' but the extract never documents an explicit methodology-selection-and-defence process or names primary-evidence generation — resolved to level 2.

W1: Studio A's (ABPL90284) hurdle-weighted final presentation to 'a panel of guest critics' is a real external-practitioner audience matching level 3's anchor, but no other core studio documents an external/guest panel and no assessment item explicitly names professional conduct or accountability as a graded criterion, so the 'assessed repeatedly and progressively... with professional conduct... explicitly among the assessed criteria' requirement is not met — resolved to level 2.

W3: The MUCH Heritage Industry Internship (ABPL90360) is a substantial, supervised, host-accountable, reflectively-assessed placement that would otherwise read as level 2 or higher, but it is one of two choices in the 'Core option' category (alternative: Minor Thesis) and so is not required of all students, matching level 1's literal 'optional internship' anchor — resolved to level 1.
